correctness.rationale: For the exact finite base u_{3,0}=0121021 and u_{3,1}=01021, all twelve circular overhang windows have explicit matching 0-based positions inside h^6(0), validated by the accompanying Python checker. For each cyclic phase, applying h to a full cyclic word plus two letters yields enough trailing length because every cyclic pair avoids 22, and a phase offset in a letter image is at most one: 3 >= 1+2. The image is a factor of p=h(p). All h-images avoid cyclic 22, enabling induction. From tile structure of the suffix code {01,21,0}, p has no 00,11,20,22; a square h^k(a)h^k(a) ending with 1 decodes right-to-left uniquely to h^{k-1}(a)h^{k-1}(a). This forces forbidden 00 or 11 at level zero. Each tower increases in length, giving infinitely many distinct Lie-positive lengths. Finite experiments do not replace the unlimited proof.

originality.rationale: The previously published definition and generic bound for Lie complexity do not entail nonzero values at the specific two substitution-tower lengths, much less that every cyclic phase has an occurring two-letter wraparound extension. The primary paper introducing this exact ternary word describes factor complexity, critical exponent, balance, Abelian complexity, bispecial factors, and a forbidden-factor characterization, without a statement equivalent to the exact simultaneous overhang inclusion. This new positive assertion is proved for all iterates rather than inferred from search failure. A previously published mathematical result concerns the different binary period-doubling morphism. The search cannot exclude unseen equivalences; the identified risks are recorded.

value.rationale: For a well-studied low-factor-complexity ternary Pisot-morphic word, the theorem simultaneously guarantees the appearance of every cyclic phase with TWO letters of periodic wraparound at every iterate in TWO natural substitution towers, despite the absence of each designated full square. It supplies a constructive infinite sequence of Lie-complexity witnesses with a stronger quantitative local cyclic property, separating near-periodic language realizability from exact-square occurrence. The exact object and invariant are intrinsically motivated by cyclic factor/Lie complexity and morphic recurrence; neither mere finite enumeration nor the already-known generic coexistence of Lie positivity with square avoidance is offered as the contribution.
